summary: Chelinda Airfield is a small high-altitude airstrip situated on the Nyika Plateau in northern Malawi, serving as the primary air gateway to Nyika National Park. The surrounding plateau rises to roughly 2,500 meters and is known for its rolling montane grasslands, rare orchids, and populations of roan antelope, zebra, and eland. Charter flights from Lilongwe and other Malawian hubs deliver visitors directly to safari lodges in this remote corner of the country.
faqs:
Q: What is Chelinda Airfield used for?
A: It primarily serves visitors heading to Nyika National Park, with charter flights connecting it to safari lodges on the plateau.

Q: Which airlines operate at Chelinda?
A: No scheduled commercial airlines serve the airstrip; access is by charter or private aircraft arranged through safari operators.

Q: What is the best time to visit the Nyika Plateau?
A: The dry season from May to October generally offers the best wildlife viewing, clearer skies, and more reliable flying conditions.

Q: Are there facilities at the airport?
A: The airfield is a basic grass strip with minimal infrastructure; passengers are typically met by lodge representatives on arrival.
transport_tips: There is no scheduled public transport to the airfield, so visitors should arrange charter flights or transfers through their safari lodge in advance. The drive from the nearest town is long and rough, taking several hours on unpaved roads, which is why most travellers fly in. Light aircraft used on this route have strict weight limits, so pack soft-sided bags and keep luggage minimal.
local_tip: Despite being in tropical Africa, temperatures on the Nyika Plateau can drop close to freezing at night year-round, so even in summer you will want a warm fleece or jacket for early-morning game drives.
